rationale:
Evidence: iteration 1 (score 37.04) still went off track in all 60 development trials, with progress only 0.04 to 0.125 and max_error at the 0.06 m off-track limit. The robot loses the line early, and the design gives it little help once it drifts.

Diagnosis: the sensor span was ±0.04 m. Once the tape sits about 0.03 m or more from centre, the outer sensors read nothing. Only near-centre sensors then see tape, so the normalised signal is small or zero and the correction is weak. The robot then drifts to the limit. Iteration 0 had the same span, so it has the same weakness.

Changes: (1) Widen the sensor array to x = ±0.075 m with 7 sensors at 0.025 m spacing, so the tape stays visible out to about 0.09 m offset. The outer edge of the 0.016 m footprints then sits inside the off-track limit. (2) Scale the weights linearly with x, so the signal is roughly proportional to lateral offset (about d/0.075) over the whole range. Weights are -1.0, -0.67, -0.33, 0, 0.33, 0.67, 1.0. (3) Because the signal is now about half as large per metre of offset, raise kp from 3.0 to 4.5 to keep similar steering authority. (4) Raise kd from 0.3 to 0.4 to keep the same damping ratio as kp rises. (5) Keep sensor size 0.016, sensor y 0.06, base_speed 1.2 (speed is the secondary issue while the robot stays on the line), mass 0.6, wheel track 0.12, wheel radius 0.03, body 0.12 by 0.16, ki 0, and line_loss last_direction.

Expected result: the robot should stay on the line through the bends, with max_error well under 0.06 and fewer line-loss events. I expect progress to rise clearly above 0.125 on the oval and s-bend, and possibly to complete some runs. Finishing in 3 s will likely need a higher base_speed in a later revision once tracking is stable.
